status.en: 17 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Mogadishu, Baidoa and Puntland.
status.nb: 17 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Mogadishu, Baidoa og Puntland.

summary.en: Fitgharan forces now control the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor while Laftagareen forces have captured Buurhakaba and another town in the Bay region, extending combat in southern Somalia. Al Shabaab detonated an IED in Mandera, injuring six civilians, and a senior al-Shabaab figure was killed by Somali intelligence. Heavy fighting erupted near Baidoa and in Burijeed as Laftagareen forces attacked army positions, prompting UN calls to halt the fighting amid famine, displacement and flood risks. Ethiopia has withdrawn more than 3,000 troops and will not intervene in the South West State conflict, and a UAE drone strike in Puntland killed four family members, including a pregnant teenager. 2,284 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Fitgharan-styrkene kontrollerer nå korridoren Mogadishu-Baidoa, mens Laftagareen-styrkene har erobret Buurhakaba og en annen by i Bay-regionen, og utvider kampene i sørlige Somalia. Al Shabaab detonerte en IED i Mandera, og seks sivile ble såret, og en høytstående al-Shabaab-person ble drept av somalisk etterretning. Kraftige kamper brøt ut nær Baidoa og i Burijeed da Laftagareen-styrkene angrep hærens posisjoner, noe som førte til FN-oppfordringer om å stoppe kampene midt i hungersnød, fordrivelse og flomrisiko. Etiopia har trukket tilbake mer enn 3 000 soldater og vil ikke intervenere i konflikten i South West State, og et droneangrep fra De forente arabiske emirater i Puntland drepte fire familiemedlemmer, inkludert en gravid tenåring. 2 284 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Somali Civil War (2009–present)
background.extract: The ongoing phase of the Somali Civil War began in 2009 and is concentrated in southern and central Somalia, primarily between the forces of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), assisted by African Union peacekeeping forces, and the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, which pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012.
